purpose: Falsifiable research hypotheses for a software-only Atmosphère path on Mariko firmware 23.0.1. Each record states what would confirm or kill it, so a negative result is recorded instead of being rediscovered.

status_legend.meaning: Directly supported by an authoritative or primary source, or reproduced under a stated procedure.
Indirect evidence, or a result that covers a related but not identical case.
Plausible and testable, but not yet tested or not independently checked.
Contradicted by an authoritative source or by a reproduced negative result.
Insufficient evidence; currently blocked, untested, or not reachable with available materials.

stage_legend.0: Trigger: obtain the software or surface the entry point lives in.
stage_legend.1: Initial code execution in an ordinary userland process.
stage_legend.2: Privilege escalation to a sysmodule with useful permissions, or to the kernel.
stage_legend.3: Boot-stage execution at warmboot or package1, before Horizon verifies its modules.
stage_legend.4: Launch and persistence of a payload or CFW.

hypotheses.title: capmtp object-read boundary validation
hypotheses.hypothesis: The PTP object-read handler may fail to bound the requested offset and length against the object size, allowing an out-of-bounds read or a crash when a host supplies boundary values.
prerequisites: USB host access to the console in Copy to PC via USB mode
A PTP session and at least one object handle
Approval to send boundary parameters
hypotheses.expected_capability: At most an out-of-bounds read from the capmtp process, which would be an information disclosure. It would not provide code execution by itself.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Enumerate storages and object handles, then issue GetObject with offset and length at 0, size-1, size, size+1, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000, and 0xFFFFFFFF. Record the response code, returned length, and whether the console stays responsive. Use scripts/ptp_boundary.py.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A successful response whose returned length exceeds the object size, or data that is inconsistent with the object's declared size, indicates a validation failure. A transport timeout or a dropped PTP interface indicates a crash or hang and must be recorded as such.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: Every boundary case returns a documented PTP error code or a response bounded by the object size, and the console remains responsive across the full run. Record the run as a negative result and stop probing this operation.
hypotheses.risks: A malformed boundary request could hang or crash capmtp. Recovery is to disconnect the cable and reboot the console. The session is read-only and no object is modified.
hypotheses.results: Closed negative on 2026-10-26. After discovery was fixed, GetObject returned 0x2006 ParameterNotSupported for all ten tested parameter sets, including a valid handle with offset 0. Object data could not be read, so the offset and length logic was never exercised. See hardware observation 2026-10-26-ptp-boundary.
hypotheses.uncertainties: GetObject may require an undocumented precondition, and GetThumb was not tested. The underlying validation logic remains unexamined; the direction is closed because the operation is not a reachable primitive.

hypotheses.title: capmtp handle-table parameter validation
hypotheses.hypothesis: GetObjectHandles and GetObjectInfo may not validate storage IDs, object format codes, parent handles, or object handles before using them to index internal state, producing an out-of-bounds read or a crash.
prerequisites: USB host access to the console in Copy to PC via USB mode
A PTP session
Approval to send invalid identifiers
hypotheses.expected_capability: An information disclosure or a denial of service in capmtp. Not code execution by itself.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Issue GetObjectHandles with invalid storage IDs, unknown format codes, and invalid parent handles, and GetObjectInfo with handles 0, 1, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000, and 0xFFFFFFFF. Record response codes and responsiveness. Use scripts/ptp_boundary.py --family handles.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A response containing handles or metadata that were never advertised, or an inconsistent success response for an invalid identifier, indicates a validation failure. A timeout indicates a crash or hang.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: All invalid identifiers return documented PTP errors and the console remains responsive. Record as a negative result.
hypotheses.risks: Same as H-001: possible capmtp hang or crash, recoverable by disconnecting and rebooting.
hypotheses.results: Tested on the target on 2026-10-26. Eight invalid-identifier cases returned documented PTP errors (0x2009 or 0x200b) and the console stayed responsive. The 0xFFFFFFFF storage/parent pair returned 14 associations, which is documented 'all' semantics. See hardware observation 2026-10-26-ptp-boundary.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Scoped to the tested identifiers. The transient endpoint stall is not attributed to this hypothesis and did not reproduce after a replug.

hypotheses.title: Mariko warmboot memory-safety bug
hypotheses.component: package1 section 0 (warmboot) and the TSEC payload on Mariko
hypotheses.hypothesis: The Mariko warmboot path on 23.0.1 may contain a memory-safety defect reachable during boot, which would allow pre-Horizon code execution and therefore a software-only CFW launch without a modchip.
prerequisites: The owner's local 23.0.1 firmware dump and matching prod.keys, kept outside version control
Extraction tooling for package1 and NCAs (hactool or equivalent)
A second firmware version for a meaningful diff
A disassembler or decompiler for the warmboot and TSEC payloads
A way to execute hypotheses in an emulator or on a sacrificial device
hypotheses.expected_capability: Boot-stage code execution, which is the decisive missing stage for Atmosphère on Mariko.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Diff package1 section 0 and the TSEC payload across firmware versions, identify parsing and bounds logic, and rank candidate defects by reachability before Horizon starts. Validate candidates in an emulator before any hardware test.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A reachable unchecked length, index, or pointer derived from boot-time data, with a plausible path from the boot state to controlled memory.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: No reachable defect survives review across the diffed versions, or every candidate requires a precondition that the boot state cannot supply.
hypotheses.risks: Firmware analysis itself is passive. Testing a candidate on hardware could brick the console and is not authorized by this project.
hypotheses.blocked_by: The dump is NCA-only and does not contain package1. The owner's keys stop at key generation 0x14, while the 23.0.1 NCAs use up to 0x17; the ldn program NCA needs key_area_key_application_16, which is absent. A package1 image would also need matching package1 key material. No hactool or nxdump is installed.
hypotheses.results: Not started. The owner supplied a local 23.0.1 firmware dump and prod.keys, but the dump is NCA-only and the keys do not cover the 23.0.1 NCA key generation, so package1 has not been decrypted or verified.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Whether the dump is complete and matches 23.0.1; whether package1 can be decrypted with the owner's keys; whether any reachable defect exists in Mariko warmboot; whether a second firmware version can be obtained lawfully; whether emulation of Mariko warmboot is accurate enough to validate a candidate.

hypotheses.title: ns2jb fs path-normalization bug on Switch 1
hypotheses.component: fs sysmodule, IFileSystem GetEntryType and Path::Normalize
hypotheses.hypothesis: Because the documented filesystem API is largely unchanged between Switch 1 and Switch 2, the path-normalization buffer overflow described in the ns2jb write-up may also exist in the Switch 1 fs sysmodule on 23.0.1.
prerequisites: A stage-1 userland primitive on Switch 1 23.0.1
Either a Switch 1 fs binary to inspect or a way to observe the behavior
hypotheses.expected_capability: Privilege escalation from a userland process to the fs sysmodule, which is stage 2. It is not an entry point and does not reach boot stage.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Compare the documented GetEntryType path handling across generations and inspect a Switch 1 fs binary for the 0x301-byte temporary buffer and the backslash parent-directory path. Confirm only with a stage-1 primitive in a controlled environment.
hypotheses.expected_signal: Presence of the same normalize-and-copy sequence with a fixed 0x301-byte allocation and no length check.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: The Switch 1 implementation uses a different normalization path, bounds the copy, or is absent.
hypotheses.risks: Testing on hardware requires a stage-1 primitive that does not exist publicly. Static inspection is passive.
hypotheses.blocked_by: No stage-1 primitive on Switch 1 23.0.1 and no Switch 1 fs binary are available.
hypotheses.results: Not tested. Blocked on a stage-1 primitive and a Switch 1 fs binary.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Whether Switch 1 fs shares the normalize-and-copy implementation; whether the 0x301-byte buffer is the same size.

hypotheses.title: Switch 1 browser WebKit n-day applicability
hypotheses.component: NetFront-based browser applets (WifiWebAuthApplet, account login) and the system web applet
hypotheses.hypothesis: The Switch 1 browser may run a WebKit build exposed to publicly known n-days, and Switch 1 lacks the pointer-authentication mitigations the ns2jb author cites for Switch 2, so a matching public bug could still yield userland code execution.
prerequisites: A way to reach the browser applet (captive portal or a title that opens it)
The browser engine version or a fingerprint
A public n-day matching that version
hypotheses.expected_capability: Userland code execution in a browser applet, which is stage 1.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Serve a controlled page through a captive-portal setup and record the user agent, JavaScript feature detection, and engine quirks to estimate the WebKit vintage. Map the result to public advisories before attempting anything further.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A browser build old enough to match a published, exploitable n-day, plus a reachable applet invocation.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: The browser build is patched for all matching public advisories, or no applet invocation can be reached without a modified console.
hypotheses.risks: Captive-portal testing changes the console's temporary network settings, which are reversible. Exploit development is out of scope and untested.
hypotheses.blocked_by: No fingerprint has been collected, and no public chain for 23.0.1 exists.
hypotheses.results: Closed negative on 2026-10-26. The applet is reachable and runs JavaScript, and the engine is feature-bracketed to Safari 15.4-15.6, but a timing probe found no JIT warm-up: a 400,000-iteration loop stayed at 39-40 ms across twelve runs and the polymorphic variant at 48-49 ms, with WebAssembly unavailable. Most public WebKit exploits rely on JIT behaviour, and no public non-JIT proof of concept was found for this bracket. The patch level also remains unknown.
hypotheses.uncertainties: A JIT could be disabled only for this applet, and timing is indirect. Non-JIT DOM or parser bugs could still exist, but none is public for this bracket and exploitation would be original research. A browser compromise would still be applet-level, not homebrew.

hypotheses.title: GameShare splay remote parsing bug
hypotheses.component: splay system applet; NACP, JPEG, and stream handling
hypotheses.hypothesis: The splay applet may mishandle host-supplied NACP or JPEG data in a way that yields memory corruption on the receiving console.
prerequisites: A Nintendo Switch 2 to host GameShare
A GameShare-compatible title
A user-initiated receive flow on the target
hypotheses.expected_capability: Applet-level userland code execution, which is stage 1 with a low privilege ceiling.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Obtain the protocol description or instrument a host, then test malformed metadata against a sacrificial receiver. This is not authorized on the target console.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A parsing fault that is reproducible and attributable to host-supplied data.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: Parsing is delegated to hardened services, or all malformed inputs are rejected before use.
hypotheses.risks: Crafting host data and sending it to a console is outside this project's authorization boundary.
hypotheses.blocked_by: No Switch 2 host and no public protocol specification.
hypotheses.results: Not tested. No Switch 2 host is available.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Protocol framing; which data the ECC signature covers; whether NACP and JPEG parsing happen before user confirmation.

hypotheses.title: Artemis save chain-load reaching native code
hypotheses.component: Artemis Engine games and their save-file script loading
hypotheses.hypothesis: An Artemis Engine title on Switch may chain-load Lua from an edited save, and the engine's Lua bindings may expose a path from script execution to native code execution.
prerequisites: An Artemis Engine title on Switch
A way to place an edited save on a stock console
Engine builds and Lua binding documentation
hypotheses.expected_capability: Game-level script execution, and only with an additional bug, native code execution. Stage 1.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Identify Switch titles using Artemis, determine whether save data can be placed on a stock console, and audit the Lua bindings for native escapes.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A documented binding that reaches native memory or FFI from game script.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: Save injection is impossible on a stock console, or the Lua environment is sandboxed with no native escape.
hypotheses.risks: Save manipulation is reversible but requires a delivery path that a stock console may not have.
hypotheses.blocked_by: No Switch reproduction and no save-delivery path on a stock console.
hypotheses.results: Documented for PS4 and Windows only; no Switch reproduction.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Whether an Artemis title exists on Switch with the same save-loading behavior; whether the Lua bindings expose native access; how a crafted save would reach a stock console.

hypotheses.title: Non-JS image decoder surface in the captive-portal applet
hypotheses.component: WebKit image decoders in WifiWebAuthApplet (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP, SVG)
hypotheses.hypothesis: The applet decodes attacker-supplied images in-process, and a decoder that predates a public fix could provide JIT-independent code execution. CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp Huffman heap overflow, fixed September 2023) is the leading candidate because the engine is a 2022 WebKit generation and does not use a JIT.
prerequisites: WebP decoding enabled in the applet
An unpatched libwebp (or another vulnerable decoder)
A crafted image delivered from the portal server
hypotheses.expected_capability: Code execution in the applet process, which is stage 1. Not SD homebrew and not kernel.
hypotheses.test_procedure: First run scripts/fingerprint_formats.html to confirm which formats decode, especially WebP. Only with explicit approval, test a public crash reproducer against the applet and record whether it faults.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A format loads successfully, establishing that its decoder is reachable. A crash or fault on a crafted file would confirm the decoder is vulnerable, not merely present.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: WebP is not decoded, or the decoder rejects the crafted input without a fault and the applet stays responsive.
hypotheses.risks: A crafted image may crash the browser applet or the console. Recovery is to exit the applet and reboot. Testing a public crash reproducer is exploit testing and needs explicit approval.
hypotheses.results: Closed inconclusive on 2026-10-26. The surface is reachable and all six image formats decode, including lossless WebP. The console decoded both CVE-2023-4863 reproducers to 1x1 images, while stock libwebp 1.2.4, 1.3.1, and 1.6.0 reject them, so the decoder is non-stock. Sixty repeated decodes of the stronger file produced no visible fault. A silent overflow cannot be excluded without ASAN, but no observable signal exists and further repeats would not add information. A sweep of stock libwebp 1.0.3 through 1.6.0 found that every release rejects both reproducers; the console accepts them, so its decoder is not stock libwebp and the CVE is likely inapplicable.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Whether the decoder wrote out of bounds silently. Confirming it would need ASAN, the decoder binary, or heap-grooming work that is indistinguishable from exploit development. No path to homebrew follows from this surface alone. The decoder may be NetFront's own implementation rather than libwebp, in which case CVE-2023-4863 does not apply at all.

hypotheses.title: SD-card FAT32 metadata parser
hypotheses.component: Console FAT32 driver and filesystem service, reached by mounting a crafted microSD image
hypotheses.hypothesis: The console's FAT32 parser may mishandle crafted filesystem metadata such as out-of-range cluster references, oversized directory entries, or cyclic chains, producing a memory-safety failure in the filesystem driver or fs service.
prerequisites: A sacrificial microSD card and reader
The console's SD slot
A crafted image that the console will mount
hypotheses.expected_capability: A fault in the FAT32 driver or fs service, which would be below userland. Stage 2 at best; it would not by itself provide boot-stage execution.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Write one anomaly image at a time to the sacrificial card, insert it into the console, and record whether the console mounts, rejects, hangs, or reboots. Start with dir_cluster_oob, then cluster_oob, dir_size_huge, fat_loop, bpb_spc_zero, lfn_bad, and two_fats_mismatch.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A hang, reboot, or filesystem-service fault when a specific anomaly is mounted, reproducible with that image and not with the control.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: Every anomaly is either rejected cleanly or mounted without a fault, and the control behaves the same as the anomalies.
hypotheses.risks: A malformed card can hang or crash the console; remove the card and reboot. The card is erased. Internal storage is not touched.
hypotheses.hardware: HEG-001 (Mariko) plus a sacrificial microSD and reader
hypotheses.results: Tested on the target on 2026-10-27. The control image mounts. An out-of-range file entry is skipped cleanly while a real file in the same directory is listed. An out-of-range Nintendo/Album directory cluster causes the Album applet to hang and report 2802-9999, a handled applet failure with no crash report. Zero sectors-per-cluster is rejected at mount with a format prompt. No memory-safety signal was observed in the tested anomalies.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Only a subset of anomalies was tested; cyclic chains and near-boundary cluster values were not. A silent fault cannot be excluded, but every tested invalid input was rejected or handled.

hypotheses.title: Post-23.0.0 LDN pre-auth parser memory-safety bug
hypotheses.component: ldn sysmodule and WLAN local-wireless authentication path
hypotheses.hypothesis: The Switch 1 23.0.1 LDN implementation may mishandle a malformed advertisement or authentication frame in a way that produces a memory-safety fault before a station is authenticated, even though CVE-2026-82079 was fixed in 23.0.0.
prerequisites: A Linux host or Linux VM with a Wi-Fi adapter that can receive and transmit action frames in monitor mode
The console in an LDN-active state, preferably a local-wireless join/scan screen
Explicit approval to transmit LDN frames
For a retail encrypted LDN network: matching prod.keys. The owner now has a local prod.keys dump from their own modded Switch; it is excluded from version control.
hypotheses.expected_capability: A fault in the ldn sysmodule or WLAN path; stage 2 at best. It would not by itself provide boot-stage execution.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Phase 0: verify the adapter and driver on the Linux host or Linux VM. Phase 1 (passive): have the console host a local-wireless room, capture advertisement frames with tcpdump, and parse the plaintext NetworkId header with scripts/ldn_probe.py. Phase 2 (active, approval required): put the console in join/scan mode, host a prod-mode LDN network with scripts/ldn_host.py using the captured title/scene/SSID/channel and the owner's local keys, and record whether the console joins. Confirm RF transmission with a second monitor-mode receiver, a phone Wi-Fi analyzer that shows hidden BSSIDs, or the CachyOS PC/mt7921e path. A directed scan for a 16-byte SSID is invalid (E-086). A wildcard CoreWLAN BSSID comparison is valid only with Location Services permission (E-092); without it, macOS returns nil BSSIDs (E-088). The monitor-mode host path on rtw88_8822bu does not transmit (E-091). The AP-mode beacon half of management-frame injection works: a test beacon sent through NL80211_CMD_FRAME was received at -28 dBm in all 12 scans (E-094). The remaining AP step is a unicast vendor action frame to a station entry for the console, because a broadcast non-public action frame is rejected with -ENOLINK (E-093); a monitor-TX-capable adapter/driver remains the fallback. Coordinate the host window with the game's roughly one-second search. Phase 3 (separate approval): if it joins, send one malformed authentication response at a time and record the console's behavior. On 2026-10-29 the AP path carried the real advertisement only with the AP BSSID; the driver rejects a broadcast-BSSID action frame with EINVAL (E-097), so the AP variant differs from the original broadcast advertisement. A supervised rerun then made the room TX10LED appear on the console, but selecting it produced 2203-0065 immediately and hostapd recorded no authentication or association event (E-098). The next test must configure hostapd with the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID and the LDN RSN IE, then answer the console's custom 0x88B7 authentication request with the derived WLAN key. On 2026-10-29 the corrected AP configuration reached open-system authentication and association (AID 1), but the console disassociated itself with reason 8 about one second later and no 0x88B7 authentication request was observed (E-099). The monitor's only console frame was a 28-byte null-data frame, not the LDN request; the AP raw socket saw a 20-byte frame with ethertype 0x0006 that is not yet identified. The next run must omit the association-response RSN IE to match the ldn package's MonitorAP, capture raw hex and a local pcap on mon-ldn, and use the authorized-station raw 0x88B7 response path because the AP control port rejects that ethertype with EINVAL (E-100).
hypotheses.expected_signal: A crash, reboot, or error report after a specific malformed frame, reproducible with that frame and not with a well-formed control.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: After host transmission is independently confirmed, the console rejects or ignores the encrypted prod-mode network and every malformed pre-auth frame, with no crash report and no loss of responsiveness; or the adapter/driver cannot capture or transmit LDN action frames and no known-good adapter or second host is available; or the firmware cannot be parsed with the available tools. Record as blocked or negative as appropriate.
hypotheses.risks: A malformed frame could hang or crash the ldn sysmodule or the Wi-Fi firmware. Recovery is to stop the host, power-cycle the console, and restart the adapter. No storage is written. Active frame injection is outside the current authorization until approved.
hypotheses.blocked_by: The current monitor-mode host path is blocked: rtw88_8822bu receives and AP-mode transmits, but monitor-mode injection does not put frames on the air (E-090, E-091). Run 3 produced valid same-phy captures (373/656 advertisements) but no join and no room; the independent Location Services-enabled scan did not see the host BSSID, although it saw a hidden ambient BSSID (E-089). The next host path must use AP-mode management-frame injection (NL80211_CMD_FRAME on an AP interface), hostapd vendor elements if the advertisement can be carried in a beacon/probe response, or a different adapter/driver with working monitor-mode TX. The ldn program NCA also remains encrypted because the key file stops at generation 0x14 (E-083). E-093 records a source-level limit on the AP path: upstream mac80211 can send a beacon through NL80211_CMD_FRAME, but a non-public vendor action frame on an AP interface needs a station entry, so a broadcast LDN action frame is rejected with -ENOLINK. The AP path therefore needs a unicast vendor action to a known console station entry, or a different adapter/driver. E-094 resolves the beacon half of the AP path: a 20-frame test beacon submitted through NL80211_CMD_FRAME on an AP interface was received by the Mac at -28 dBm in all 12 scans. The remaining AP limit is the vendor action frame: E-093 requires a station entry, so the next test must use a unicast vendor action to the console's station MAC, or a different adapter/driver. E-095 shows the kernel accepts the unicast action path: a temporary station entry for the console's MAC was added, five unicast vendor actions with a non-LDN OUI were submitted without a netlink error, and the station entry was removed. The remaining question is whether the console's LDN parser reacts to a real LDN vendor action sent this way, which needs a new approved AP-mode prod-mode run. On 2026-10-29 the real LDN unicast run sent 568 valid advertisements and 568 null-SSID beacons with the AP BSSID, all accepted by the kernel, but the console was off/away, so the run is inconclusive for reception (E-096). The driver rejects a broadcast-BSSID action frame with EINVAL (E-097), so the AP path can only send the AP-BSSID variant. A supervised rerun on 2026-10-29 made the room appear, but the console rejected the join immediately with 2203-0065 and hostapd saw no authentication or association (E-098). The next step is a corrected AP configuration: hostapd must use the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID and the LDN RSN IE, and a userspace responder must answer the console's custom 0x88B7 authentication request with the derived WLAN key. The current hostapd configuration cannot complete that exchange. The corrected AP configuration then reached authentication and association, but the console disassociated with reason 8 before the LDN exchange (E-099). The association response included an RSN IE that the ldn MonitorAP does not send; that mismatch is the leading candidate. The next run must omit the association-response RSN IE, capture raw frames, and use the raw authorized-station response path (E-100). If the console still leaves before 0x88B7, record D9 as negative rather than repeating the same host configuration. The current hostapd/AP path is exhausted for this adapter: three supervised AP-mode runs reached at most authentication and association, and the third run with the association-response RSN IE omitted still disassociated before 0x88B7 (E-101). No console data payload frame was observed. The remaining host-side differences are implementation details (beacon SSID encoding, capability/IE set, hostapd versus MonitorAP), not evidence of a console vulnerability. D9 is negative for this host path; further progress needs static analysis of the ldn NCA with the missing key generation, a different adapter/driver with working monitor-mode TX, or a different surface.
hypotheses.hardware: HEG-001 (Mariko), macOS 26.3 host with an OrbStack Ubuntu 26.04 arm64 VM and a TP-Link Archer T3U Plus (2357:0138, rtw88_8822bu) passed through to the VM
hypotheses.results: Phase 0 and Phase 1 completed on 2026-10-28. The adapter supports monitor mode and captured 269 frames. The console, while hosting a Dragon Ball FighterZ local-wireless room, emitted 64 LDN advertisement frames for title 0100a250097f0000, scene 0, LDN version 4, AES-CTR format, channel 1. The plaintext NetworkId header was parsed without keys. Phase 2 was approved once and executed on 2026-10-28. The first setup failed because rtw88_8822bu rejects NL80211_MNTR_FLAG_ACTIVE; a --compat-no-active-ack path created the ACK monitor without the flag. A 2-second diagnostic and a 30-second plaintext host run started and stopped cleanly, but the console showed no room, the host logged no JOIN, and no authentication request was observed. dmesg reported 'failed to get tx report from firmware', so host transmission was unconfirmed; the run was inconclusive, not a clean rejection of security mode 3. The owner then supplied prod.keys and a 23.0.1 NCA-only dump; the keys decrypt the Phase 1 advertisement (security mode 1, challenge enabled, max 2, app version 26). On 2026-10-28/29 the host was extended to security mode 1 and run for 30 seconds with the captured title/scene/SSID/channel. It emitted 373 AES-CTR advertisements captured on the existing monitor interface (655 on the ldn interface), and the first frame decrypted to the same fields as the Phase 1 room. The host logged no JOIN; the console reported no rooms after a roughly one-second search; the captures saw no frames from the console. The same-phy capture may include loopback, so RF transmission is not independently confirmed. The directed CoreWLAN scan is invalid: it returned FOUND for a random non-existent 16-byte SSID with a nil BSSID. A wildcard scan for the host BSSID is the next independent check. CVE-2026-82079 is fixed in 23.0.0; no 23.0.1 parser bug is known. The ldn program NCA remains encrypted because the key file stops at generation 0x14. On 2026-10-28/29 a second approved prod-mode run repeated the test with the console search triggered after the host was already advertising. The host logged 'Advertising now' and again ended with 'Join events observed: 0.' The console again reported no rooms. The wrapper's tcpdump processes failed with 'Permission denied' on the previous tcpdump-owned pcap files, so there is no valid run-2 capture; the summary's frame counts are from run 1. dmesg TX-report failures increased from 4 to 5. Ten wildcard CoreWLAN scans during the run all reported 'BSSID not found in 8 scan result(s)', but a post-run control scan showed that macOS returned a nil BSSID for every one of 10 ambient networks, so the comparison is invalid rather than negative (E-088). The repeat run is therefore inconclusive and identifies two tooling defects: the wrapper's pcap cleanup and the macOS BSSID redaction. On 2026-10-29 a third approved prod-mode run used the fixed wrapper, a unique pcap path, and a Location Services-enabled independent CoreWLAN scan. The host advertised for 30 seconds and again logged no JOIN; the console again reported no rooms. The wrapper captured 777 packets on the existing monitor interface and 1,373 on the ldn interface; the probe found 373 and 656 AES-CTR advertisements for title 0100a250097f0000, scene 0. dmesg TX-report failures rose from 5 to 6. The Mac ran 20 wildcard scans and did not see the host BSSID, but it did see a hidden ambient BSSID on channel 1. The captures contained only the host's own frames and no ambient beacons; each injected frame appeared as a radiotap pair with txflags=0x0. An AP-mode control proved the adapter can transmit: hostapd's TX10LED-TEST beacon on channel 1 was received at -32 dBm. A monitor-mode control using the ldn package's MonitorAP beaconed TX10LED-MON for 12 seconds but was not seen by the Mac. The monitor-mode host path is therefore blocked by the driver's monitor-mode TX path, not by the console's response. The next host path should use AP-mode management-frame injection or a different adapter/driver. On 2026-10-29 an approved AP-mode control tested NL80211_CMD_FRAME on an AP interface. hostapd 2.11 reached AP-ENABLED with TX10LED-TEST on channel 1. Firmware/ap_frame_test.py then submitted 20 TX10LED-APINJ beacons at 100 ms intervals through NL80211_CMD_FRAME; all requests returned without a netlink error. Twelve Location Services-enabled CoreWLAN scans all saw both TX10LED-APINJ and TX10LED-TEST at -28 dBm on channel 1 with the adapter BSSID, while ambient networks remained visible. The adapter was restored to monitor mode. This proves the AP-mode beacon half of management-frame injection reaches the air (E-094). A source review then showed that a non-public vendor action frame on an AP interface needs a station entry; a broadcast destination is not a station, so a broadcast LDN vendor action is rejected with -ENOLINK (E-093). The next AP test is a unicast vendor action to the console's station MAC, which requires new explicit approval. A follow-up approved unicast control then added a temporary station entry for the console's MAC (recovered locally from the Phase 1 pcap) and submitted five unicast vendor actions with the non-LDN test OUI 00:11:22 on channel 1. NL80211_CMD_NEW_STATION succeeded, all five NL80211_CMD_FRAME requests returned without a netlink error, and the station entry was removed. The adapter was restored to monitor mode. This confirms the kernel-level station-lookup half of the AP path that E-093 predicted (E-095). It does not show that the console received the frame or that its LDN parser reacted; the test used a non-LDN OUI and no independent capture. dmesg again reported 'failed to get tx report from firmware'. On 2026-10-29 the owner approved a 60-second real LDN unicast test. The first attempt sent 0 advertisements because the driver rejected the broadcast-BSSID action frame with EINVAL. A diagnostic isolated the rejection: both the 1,388-byte LDN frame and a 42-byte control failed with a broadcast BSSID and succeeded with the AP BSSID (E-097); all beacon variants, including the 89-byte null-SSID LDN beacon, were accepted. The rerun used the AP BSSID and sent 568 valid AES-CTR advertisements plus 568 null-SSID LDN beacons at 100 ms intervals; all requests returned without a netlink error, the station entry was removed, and monitor mode was restored (E-096). The console was off/away during the first run, so the room appearance and parser reaction were not observed; that run is inconclusive for the LDN hypothesis. dmesg reported 'failed to get tx report from firmware' and, after hostapd stopped, a firmware download failure; the adapter required a USB deauthorize/reauthorize cycle before it probed cleanly again. A supervised rerun on 2026-10-29 made the room TX10LED appear on the console; selecting it produced 2203-0065 immediately, the search screen closed, and the console returned to the game normally. The hostapd log contains only AP-ENABLED and AP-DISABLED, with no authentication, association, or station event. The run therefore confirms that the AP-BSSID unicast advertisement reaches the console's scan path, but the join failed before hostapd saw an association. The hostapd SSID was TX10LED-TEST with open security, not the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID with the LDN RSN IE, so the immediate failure is consistent with a host-configuration mismatch rather than a parser fault (E-098). A second supervised run on 2026-10-29 used the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID and the LDN RSN IE. The console authenticated, associated with AID 1, and was marked authorized; hostapd logged AP-STA-CONNECTED. About one second later the console sent a disassociation with reason_code=8, hostapd logged AP-STA-DISCONNECTED, and the station was later deauthenticated due to inactivity. The harness sent 54 advertisements, received 0 0x88B7 auth frames, and ended with joined=False. The monitor saw one 28-byte console data frame consistent with a null-data frame, not the 946-byte auth request; the AP raw socket saw one 20-byte frame with ethertype 0x0006. The owner observed 2203-0066 after a few seconds and a game popup 'unable to join the room'; the console returned to the game normally (E-099). A local control then showed that the AP control port rejects 0x88B7 with EINVAL while the raw authorized-station path transmits it protected with KeyID 0 (E-100). A third supervised run on 2026-10-29 omitted the association-response RSN IE to match the ldn MonitorAP. The console again authenticated, associated with AID 1, and was marked authorized, then sent one 28-byte null-data frame and disassociated with reason_code=8 about 1.4 seconds after association, before any 0x88B7 request. The monitor pcap contained no console data payload frame. Omitting the association-response RSN IE did not change the outcome, so that mismatch is not the cause (E-101). The console showed 2203-0066 again and the game displayed 'unable to join the room'.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Whether the host's frames were actually on air; the same-phy capture may be loopback and the rtw88_8822bu driver still reports TX-report failures. Whether the console's one-second search overlapped the host's advertisement window; whether it scans a different channel; whether it filters the room for a reason not visible in the advertisement; whether retail 23.0.1 accepts a PC-hosted prod-mode network. Whether a prod-mode host changes the station-side parser surface; whether the parser is in the ARM ldn sysmodule or the Wi-Fi chip firmware; whether the 23.0.0 fix is complete; whether any post-fix bug exists. The owner's keys cover the LDN advertisement key derivation but not the 23.0.1 NCA key generation. Whether a second monitor-mode receiver, a phone Wi-Fi analyzer, or the CachyOS PC/mt7921e path will show the host BSSID or decode its frames. Whether macOS can expose BSSIDs with Location Services permission or a different API. Whether the wrapper's capture failure hid a real transmission or a real absence. Whether the LDN advertisement can be carried in a hostapd vendor element; whether a different adapter/driver (mt7921e or an out-of-tree rtl88x2bu build) supports monitor-mode TX; whether the console's null-SSID beacon is filtered by macOS even when a normal hidden BSSID is visible. Whether the console's LDN parser reacts to a real LDN vendor action sent to the station entry, and whether the AP's null-SSID beacon plus a unicast action frame is enough to make the room appear. Whether the console's LDN parser accepts an AP-BSSID unicast advertisement when the original room advertisement uses a broadcast BSSID; whether the 568 accepted frames were on air; whether the post-run firmware download failure affected the first run. The supervised rerun answered the room-appearance question: the room appeared, so the AP-BSSID advertisement is accepted by the scan path (E-098). The remaining questions are whether the console will associate when the AP uses the room's 32-character hexadecimal SSID and RSN IE, whether the console's 0x88B7 authentication request is protected with the derived WLAN key, whether a userspace AP can install that key and answer the challenge in time, and whether the 2203-0065 error changes once the WLAN parameters match. Whether the association-response RSN IE caused the console to leave (answered: no; E-101); whether the console sent the 0x88B7 request before it disassociated; whether the 20-byte ethertype 0x0006 frame is a null frame, an EAPOL artifact, or something else; whether the console requires the association response to contain only supported rates, as the ldn MonitorAP does; whether the raw authorized-station response path is accepted by the console's LDN client; and whether the 2203-0066 error changes when the association-response RSN IE is omitted (answered: no; E-101). Whether hostapd's zero-length beacon SSID (instead of the ldn MonitorAP's 32 zero bytes) causes the console to leave; whether hostapd's capability information, extended-capabilities IE, or WLAN state machine differs from the reference MonitorAP in a way the console rejects; whether the interrupted third run would have behaved differently after eight seconds; and whether a different adapter/driver with working monitor-mode TX would reach 0x88B7.

hypotheses.title: General 802.11 management and EAPOL parser
hypotheses.component: wlan sysmodule and Wi-Fi firmware; beacon, probe response, association response, and WPA2 EAPOL-Key handling
hypotheses.hypothesis: The Switch 1 23.0.1 Wi-Fi stack may mishandle a malformed 802.11 management information element or EAPOL-Key frame while scanning, associating, or rekeying, producing a memory-safety fault in the wlan sysmodule or the Wi-Fi firmware.
prerequisites: The TP-Link Archer T3U Plus in AP mode with hostapd, which is confirmed to transmit beacons (E-090, E-094)
A dedicated test SSID that the console will join
A same-phy capture path or hostapd logs to attribute each frame
Explicit approval for each active case batch
hypotheses.expected_capability: A fault in the wlan sysmodule or Wi-Fi firmware. This is stage 1-2 at best; it is not boot-stage execution.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Phase 1 establishes a normal open and WPA2 association and records the control. Phase 2 injects one malformed beacon IE at a time through NL80211_CMD_FRAME, then tests probe-response and association-response vendor IEs through hostapd where the stock path permits it. Phase 3 sends one malformed EAPOL-Key frame per association through NL80211_CMD_CONTROL_PORT_FRAME after a clean control rekey. Every batch uses 25 beacons at 200 ms or one EAPOL frame per association, with a well-formed control. See docs/WIFI-NETWORK-TEST-PLAN.md.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A disconnect that does not recover, an error code not seen in the control, a hang, a reboot, or a crash report after one specific frame and not after the control.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: The control associates and the console processes the control frame, but every malformed case in the approved batch is rejected cleanly and the console remains responsive, with no crash report. Record the batch as negative. If the console cannot associate or the host cannot transmit the required frame, record the phase as blocked rather than negative.
hypotheses.risks: A malformed management or EAPOL frame could hang or crash the wlan sysmodule or the Wi-Fi firmware. Recovery is to stop hostapd, restore the adapter, and power-cycle the console. No storage is written. Active frame injection is outside the current authorization until a specific batch is approved.
hypotheses.hardware: HEG-001 (Mariko), macOS 26.3 host with an OrbStack Ubuntu 26.04 arm64 VM and a TP-Link Archer T3U Plus (2357:0138, rtw88_8822bu) passed through to the VM
hypotheses.results: Not tested. The gated plan is drafted; no active management or EAPOL frames have been sent.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Whether a normal WPA2 association completes on the test AP; whether the console processes an injected EAPOL-Key rekey; whether the malformed IE reaches the wlan parser or is filtered by the Wi-Fi firmware; whether the parser is in the ARM sysmodule or the firmware; whether any post-23.0.0 defect exists.

hypotheses.title: DHCP, DNS, IPv6, and TLS network-stack parser
hypotheses.component: bsdsocket, sfdnsres, nifm/bsdcfg DHCP client, IPv6 neighbor discovery, and the ssl sysmodule (NSS)
hypotheses.hypothesis: The Switch 1 23.0.1 network stack may mishandle malformed DHCP, DNS, IPv6 router-advertisement/neighbor-discovery, or TLS handshake/certificate data, producing a memory-safety fault in a network sysmodule.
prerequisites: A test AP that provides DHCP, DNS, and optionally IPv6 service
A console that completes the built-in Test Connection flow
A local TLS listener and, for Phase 6, an approved DNS sinkhole for the connectivity-test hostname
Explicit approval for each active case batch
hypotheses.expected_capability: A fault in bsdsocket, sfdnsres, nifm/bsdcfg, or ssl. This is stage 1-2 at best; it is not boot-stage execution.
hypotheses.test_procedure: Phase 1 records the normal DHCP lease, DNS queries, and TLS endpoint. Phase 4 sends one malformed DHCP option or DNS field per Test Connection attempt. Phase 5 sends one malformed IPv6 RA/ND option per second for 10 seconds only if the console uses IPv6. Phase 6 serves one malformed TLS record or certificate per connection through a local listener. Every batch has a well-formed control. See docs/WIFI-NETWORK-TEST-PLAN.md.
hypotheses.expected_signal: A hang, reboot, crash report, new error code, or loss of network service after one specific response and not after the control.
hypotheses.kill_criteria: The control completes, but every malformed response in the approved batch is rejected or ignored cleanly and the console remains responsive, with no crash report. Record the batch as negative. If the console never reaches the parser, record the phase as blocked rather than negative.
hypotheses.risks: A malformed network response could hang or crash a network sysmodule and may leave the console's test network unusable until it is deleted. Recovery is to stop the host, delete the test SSID, and power-cycle the console. No internal storage is written. Phase 6 must not capture credentials or proxy account/eShop traffic.
hypotheses.hardware: HEG-001 (Mariko), macOS 26.3 host with an OrbStack Ubuntu 26.04 arm64 VM and a TP-Link Archer T3U Plus (2357:0138, rtw88_8822bu) passed through to the VM
hypotheses.results: Not tested. The gated plan is drafted; no crafted DHCP, DNS, IPv6, or TLS responses have been sent.
hypotheses.uncertainties: Whether the console uses IPv6 on the test AP; whether the TLS connectivity-test flow reaches a local listener; whether malformed data reaches the parser before certificate or protocol validation; whether the 23.0.0 bsdsocket fix covers the tested AddrInfo paths; whether the ssl sysmodule uses a patched NSS build.
